title: Exploring the Boundaries of Content Moderation in Text-to-Image Generation
findings: The study audited T2I models for content moderation on prompts related to religion. It found that prompts for a 'person reading the Koran in public' and a 'fundamentalist Muslim' were subject to content moderation by at least one of the audited models, while other prompts depicting different religious attire or practices were not. This suggests potential over-censorship or bias in how certain religious contexts, particularly related to Islam, are handled by content moderation systems.
